import re

# Test cases
test_cases = """
2024-01-15 Some text 192.168.1.1 more text 2024-02-28
2024-03-15 Another line 10.0.0.1
No IP here 2024-01-15
2024-06-15 Line with two IPs 172.16.0.1 and 192.168.0.1 2024-07-20
user 1134-12-1234 should not match
2024-02-29 Leap year date 192.168.1.1
2024-02-30 Invalid date no match 192.168.1.1
0000-01-01 Year zero 1.1.1.1
2024-12-31 Last of year 255.255.255.255
text-2024-01-15 date preceded by text 192.168.1.1
2024-01-15-text date followed by text 192.168.1.1
"""

# Build the regex
# IPv4: 0-255 without leading zeros
# Octet 0-9: just digit
# Octet 10-99: 1-9 followed by 0-9
# Octet 100-199: 1 followed by 0-9 twice
# Octet 200-249: 2 followed by 0-4 followed by 0-9
# Octet 250-255: 25 followed by 0-5

octet = r'(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9][0-9]|[0-9])'
ipv4 = r'(?<![0-9a-zA-Z])(' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r')(?![0-9a-zA-Z])'

# Date: YYYY-MM-DD
# Year: 0000-9999
# Month: 01-09,10-12
# Day: 01-28 (always safe), 29 (only in Feb with our relaxed rule), 30 (not Feb), 31 (not Feb,Apr,Jun,Sep,Nov)

# For relaxed Feb (up to 29 days): 01-29
day_29 = r'(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9])'
day_30 = r'(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9]|30)'
day_31 = r'(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])'

month_31 = r'(?:0[13578]|1[02])'  # Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Aug, Oct, Dec
month_30 = r'(?:0[469])'  # Apr, Jun, Sep, Nov
month_29 = r'02'  # Feb

day_valid_for_month = r'(?:(' + month_31 + r')' + day_31 + r'|(' + month_30 + r')' + day_30 + r'|(' + month_29 + r')' + day_29 + r')'
year = r'[0-9]{4}'
month = r'(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])'

# Simpler date regex with proper day validation
date_simple = r'[0-9]{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])'

# Full pattern: line must contain IPv4, and we capture the last date
# We use a lookahead to ensure IPv4 exists, then capture the last date
# The trick: match everything, capture the last date, and verify IPv4 is present

# Strategy: Use a pattern that captures the last date on a line that has IPv4
# We'll use: (?=.*<ipv4>).*<last-date>
# But we need to capture just the date, not the whole match

# Actually, re.findall returns all captured groups, not the whole match
# So we can use: lookbehind for start, lookahead for ipv4, capture date

# The cleanest approach: use a pattern that matches the whole line, 
# verifies IPv4 exists somewhere, and captures the last date
pattern = r'^(?=.*(?<![0-9a-zA-Z])' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'(?![0-9a-zA-Z])).*(?<![0-9a-zA-Z])([0-9]{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9]|3[01]))(?![0-9a-zA-Z])$'

# Even simpler - since the last date needs to be captured and we're using findall:
# We can use a non-capturing group for the IPv4 check, and capture only the date
pattern2 = r'(?m)(?=.*(?<![0-9a-zA-Z])' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'\.' + octet + r'(?![0-9a-zA-Z])).*(?<![0-9a-zA-Z])([0-9]{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-9]|3[01]))(?![0-9a-zA-Z])'

print("Testing pattern2:")

print(f"Found {len(matches)} matches:")
for m in matches:

192.168.1.1 2024-01-15 IP before date
2024-01-15 2024-02-20 192.168.1.1 two dates before IP
2024-01-15 192.168.1.1 2024-02-20 date, IP, date (should match Feb 20)

2024-01-15 999.999.999.999 invalid IP no match
2024-01-15 192.168.1.256 invalid IP no match
2024-01-15 0192.168.1.1 leading zero in octet - this is tricky
"""

print("\nMore tests with pattern2:")
